rounds.proof_sketch: Kernel launches with threads_per_block=256 (1D), so blockDim.z=1 and threadIdx.z=0 for ALL threads. Original condition (threadIdx.x==0) is true for 1 thread; mutated condition (threadIdx.z==0) is true for all 256 threads. All threads read same shared_data[0], compute identical rsqrtf result, write identical value. Race condition is harmless since all writes are identical.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes which threads execute the inv_std computation from a single thread (thread 0) to all 256 threads. However, because all threads read the same input value from shared_data[0] (the variance sum from the previous reduction), perform identical deterministic floating-point operations, and write the identical result back, the race condition produces the correct value. The subsequent __syncthreads() ensures all writes complete before any thread reads the result. The net effect is redundant computation but identical output.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant is unkillable under the fixed configuration. The 1D thread block launch (blockDim.z=1) makes threadIdx.z always equal 0, causing all threads to enter the if-block. Since they all compute and write the same value, no input can produce different outputs.
rounds.recommendations: When mutation testing thread index comparisons, verify the actual thread block dimensions. Mutations swapping threadIdx.x to threadIdx.z are only effective when blockDim.z > 1. Consider adding assertions or compile-time checks that enforce expected thread block dimensions.
